scoring.initial: Box wholly loose, both ears in insertion state, cutout empty.
scoring.partial: 0.25 only box supported in cutout with flange contact and at least one ear mechanically behind wall;0.5 both ears behind wall;0.75 both contact rear gypsum but one side flange gap exceeds1mm. These are proposed physical test thresholds.
scoring.full: Both ears bear behind intact drywall, flange gap<=1mm at four corners, box orientation within3degrees of cutout and no motion under a declared5N outward manual pull after robot release; photograph front/rear, feeler gauge and spring scale.5N is benchmark check, not electrical-code certification.
scoring.invalid: Broken wall/pulled-through ears, detached screw/ear, box wedged by foreign part, cutout enlargement or fixture moved over5mm zero all credit.
scoring.reset: Undo both screws to insertion state, verify ears/gypsum intact and reposition box/tool; replace damaged coupon.
wrong_solutions: Wedge box in cutout with ears still folded: rear inspection and pull test exclude.
Deploy only one ear and tilt box: both-ear contact and four-corner gaps exclude.
Hold box flush with gripper or driver: release and independent pull test exclude.
Strip screw or crush gypsum to fake flushness: integrity gate excludes.

extension_deep_candidates.title: Focus and lock an OpenMV robot-vision camera lens

importance.person: Robot developer/electronics technician equipping an ArduPilot/PixHawk vision system.
importance.exact_workflow: Manufacturer firmware v4.5.6 includes MAVLink opticalflow sent to ArduPilot/PixHawk for position control. Same tag AprilTag3D example explicitly supports M7/OV7725 with2.8mm lens; official hardware setup requires manual focus and subsequent lock before ready for use.
importance.useful_outcome: Raw image features are sharp at the intended robot viewing distance and stay focused after release/transport. This can commission a real robot sensor, not an arbitrary camera labelled robot.
importance.objection: Generic camera optics is not automatically robot building; source establishes actual manufacturer robot-controller integration. Exact operating distance must be chosen for the intended deployment, not detuned to near macro focus for difficulty.

source_facts.procedure: Set screw not fully in; screw lens in until OpenMV IDE image sharp; tighten set screw. Explicitly the screw forms a bump in plastic preventing unscrewing, rather than digging into lens threads.
source_facts.optical_dimensions_verified: M7/OV7725+2.8mm lens, active sensor3.984x2.952mm in same-release manufacturer3D-AprilTag sample.
source_facts.image_verified: Manufacturer M7OV7725 pinout photograph inspected: plastic threaded holder, upper/back setscrew and two fastening ears. Manufacturer lens-mount front/back/quarter detail photos independently inspected; threads and closed polymer wall visible.
source_facts.unmapped_drawings: Manufacturer cam-dimensions images show1.40x1.75inch board class. Exact revision mapping is not explicit, so no M7 dimension claim from them.
source_facts.rejected_incompatible_claim: MAVLink AprilTag sample has OV5650 width/height constants. Those are NOT used as M7 evidence. Luxonis OAK/RPi HQ dimensions are NOT substituted for OpenMV parts.
source_facts.pins: openmv-doc f53f84c938fde32bc80d45919c536d651282f209; firmware v4.5.6=89478be5fb0d23596e3c0b01e655ce492e50f00c; media92fe602f4693cbc9c53f2b9dd7bfec2439963e77. Per-file SHA256 in extension-source-manifest.json.

inventory.actual_components: OpenMV Cam M7 with OV7725 sensor, its original standard2.8mm lens and polymer lens mount with actual set screw. No replacement giant ring or custom grip tabs.
inventory.materials_sizes: PCB, glass optical parts, polymer threaded holder, metal screws. Lens focal length/sensor active area verified; barrel outer diameter/projection, screw pitch, body mass, holder wall section and clamp stiffness not dimension-verified.12–15mm barrel and35x45mm board are class estimates only.
inventory.installed_initial_state: Lens holder already fixed to actual PCB with original two screws; clean sensor, real lens thread engaged but deliberately out of focus within allowable travel; real set screw loosened. Camera PCB supported by its normal mounting holes on a passive electronics fixture, USB connected with strain relief.

Chart/camera fiducials make pose changes measurable. A display shows raw camera frame during work; the target is outside arm workspace.
inventory.tools: Normal small Phillips screwdriver matching photographed head, on a passive rest; no custom fingers, no rigid fake focus knob.
inventory.mating_retention: True axial motion from real lens threads, and screw-driven local deformation/contact of plastic holder giving real friction retention. Exact thread/holder dimensions still to resolve or defensibly estimate from source.

extension_deep_candidates.instruction: Focus the robot camera on the fixed target at its marked operating distance, lock the lens with its set screw, and let go.
extension_deep_candidates.essential_ability: Grasp/rotate a small optical barrel without torquing its PCB or covering the useful image, refine optical feedback, then preserve focus while a second hand tightens its physical polymer clamp.
extension_deep_candidates.bimanual_challenge: One arm can counterhold barrel/holder against driver reaction while the second acquires and engages the driver; may need alternate barrel turns, image checks and locking. Camera fixture reacts PCB loads, not lens rotation. This is a planning hypothesis, not a tested mandatory two-hand sequence.

physical_scoring.initial: Target and camera fixed/marked, initial raw focus below threshold; lens installed with lock loose.
physical_scoring.partial: Proposed0.25 if normalized slanted-edge MTF50 reaches>=0.5 of physical best-focus reference at same exposure/target;0.5 if>=0.8 but clamp does not retain. Full sharpness measured after arms release.
physical_scoring.full: Proposed1.0: raw MTF50>=0.8 reference, neither hand supporting, set screw engaged, and lens changes<=2degrees with<5percent MTF50 loss under declared0.2N tangential spring-scale check at measured barrel radius. Torque/radius and thresholds are benchmark design choices, not manufacturer specs; choose low nondamaging load after source/fixture check.
physical_scoring.measurement: Raw saved camera image and ordinary slanted-edge analysis, close photograph of screw/barrel witness mark and spring scale. Not hidden lens-position flag or commanded-turn count.
physical_scoring.invalid: Permanent zero for damaged PCB/holder/lens, changed chart distance or camera fixture beyond5mm/2degrees, foreign locking adhesive/prop, optical contamination or broken mount.
physical_scoring.reset: Loosen setscrew, turn lens by documented small test offset to defocus without exposing sensor or bottoming thread, restore camera/chart poses and tool. No consumables if polymer clamp survives; inspect wear.

YAM.status: PLANNING PLAUSIBILITY ONLY; no robot/task instantiated and no clearance claimed.
YAM.grasp: Pinch actual barrel outer rim without gripping glass; source photograph shows only short projection, so stable pad purchase is uncertain.
YAM.palm_wrist: Source-static fingers each span~68mm laterally/~94mm axially, but those are whole visual bounds, not pad widths. All315 collision hulls per arm plus palm/wrist/elbow and tool/camera paths need test.
YAM.tools: Acquire ordinary long-shaft precision driver with normal grip; maintain actual Phillips engagement and axial load. No source torque capacity proof.
YAM.reaction: Passive PCB mounting-hole fixture reacts force; barrel counterhold avoids twisting board or losing sharpness while lock bends plastic.
YAM.paths: Approach lens from front/sides; the pads must leave a central optical cone clear during adjustments. Driver comes from top/back of holder while other hand clears screw port. Release and regrip need real-image checks.
YAM.known_risks: Tiny12mm-class barrel, light PCB, camera/FOV occlusion, tool/second-hand crowding. Nominal aperture alone is insufficient.

fidelity.preserve: Helical lens translation, sensor-relative optical conjugate, real surface contact and screw pressing local polymer wall against barrel so friction reacts torque.
fidelity.possible_approximations: Source-informed rigid optical barrel plus helical constraint; locally compliant holder wall on elastic articulation instead of full polymer FEA; physically computed defocus kernel from lens/sensor/target geometry. These are proposed faithful approximations, not executed proof.
fidelity.forbidden: A generic rotation knob replacing barrel, automatic latch from screw turns, invisible attachment or an image blur flag unrelated to physical optics/pose.
fidelity.optical_model: Thin-lens defocus may approximate central high-contrast target at working distance; validate against measured sharpness ordering before using pixel MTF. Global focus score based only on angular proximity deletes image feedback and is insufficient.
